newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuanian parliament okays sale of telecom firm.
newsitem.headline: Lithuanian parliament okays sale of telecom firm.

text.p: Lithuania's parliament voted on Thursday to allow the privatisation of Lithuanian Telecom, Lithuanian Sea Shipping and oil exploration firm Geonafta.
Deputies voted to remove these companies from a list of firms banned from sale until 2000 but left Lithuanian Railways and Lithuanian Gas on the list.

European Affairs Minister Laime Andrikiene, who has been given responsibility for the right-wing government's privatisation programme, said the gas and railway companies might be included at a later date.
"This vote was a test to parliament and the government is happy that parliament supported the radical economic reforms of the government," she told Reuters.
"It does not mean that Lithuanian Gas and railways will not be privatised earlier (than 2000). I think those companies will be excluded from this list this year," she added.
Parliament also approved the sale of the Kedainiai chemicals plant and the Panevezys Glass company.

The new government of Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius has pledged to open Lithuania's economy up to foreign investment after the country gained the reputation of being an economic laggard under the previous government of reform Communists.
